cards.explanation: The answer is Nazareth, friends. Luke 1:26 says God sent Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth. That's where the visit happens. I spent years in a junk drawer, so a town in Galilee sounds like a big upgrade to me.

The answer is Mary, friends. Luke 1:27 says the virgin's name was Mary, and she was pledged in marriage to Joseph. That's who Gabriel is sent to. Remember that name, bakers, because it's about to matter a whole lot.

The answer is False, friends. Luke 1:29 says Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be. An angel shows up with a big greeting, and she stops to think about it. Not calm at all, and I can respect that.

The answers are son and Jesus, friends. Luke 1:31 says, “…you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus.” That's the news Gabriel brings her, and he hands Mary the name before the baby is even born. It's a lot to take in, and it's only verse 31.

The answer is The Son of the Most High, bakers. Luke 1:32 says, “He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High.” Gabriel is not shy with the big titles. He's piling them on, and I'm taking notes with my mustache.

The answer is False, bakers. Luke 1:33 says, “…and He will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end!” Forever means forever. I've had a batch of cookies last about ten minutes, so forever is hard for me to picture.

The answer is “How can this be since I am a virgin,” friends. In Luke 1:34, Mary asks the angel, “How can this be… since I am a virgin?” It's a real question, asked plainly. And Gabriel answers it, which is the best part.

The answer is the Holy Spirit, bakers. Luke 1:35 says, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.” Gabriel gives Mary a real answer to her real question. I love an angel who answers the question.

The answer is Elizabeth, friends. Luke 1:36 says, “Look, even Elizabeth your relative has conceived a son in her old age, and she who was called barren is in her sixth month.” Gabriel gives Mary a real example she can point to.
The answer is True, bakers. Luke 1:37 says, “For no word from God will ever fail.” Gabriel says it right after pointing to Elizabeth. That's a line worth writing on the inside of your apron.

The answer is “I am the Lord's servant,” friends. Luke 1:38 says, “I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May it happen to me according to your word.” She heard the whole thing and said that. I think that's a lot of faith in one short sentence.
